about: Key-accuracy sample of the v2 bench decks (TASK-33c15). Run inside Kiro by the lesson-checker persona (.kiro/agents/lesson-checker.md); read-only; an AI review, not a teacher's. Not a classroom study.
rule: keyReviewSample in scripts/bench-lib.ts: every 5th objective in bench/objectives.json order starting at the 1st (positions 1, 6, 11, … 51); if that objective has no first-try file, the next objective in order that has one and is not already picked (y4-electricity-2 → y4-electricity-3); plus y3-rocks-2 (v1 had a wrong key there).
verdicts: correct = the marked answer is the one defensibly right answer; wrong = the marked answer is false or another answer is the right one; ambiguous = more than one answer is defensible, or the question cannot be answered as written.

cards.question: Which part of the plant takes in water from the soil?
What is the main job of the leaves?
Which part of the plant makes the seeds?
Which part of the plant carries water up from the roots to the leaves?
What is the main job of a flower?
cards.key: To make seeds for new plants

cards.question: What is the job of a skeleton?
cards.key: To support and protect the body

cards.question: Which body part does a muscle join to a bone?
Which part of the body protects the heart and lungs?
Which of these animals has a skeleton inside its body?
What do muscles need to pull on to make a bone move?
What happens to light when it hits a mirror?
cards.key: It bounces back off the mirror

cards.question: Which surface reflects light best?
Why can you see your face in a shiny spoon?
cards.key: Light reflects off the spoon into your eyes

cards.question: Which of these is the best reflector of light?
What do we call light bouncing off a surface?
You push a football with your foot. Do your foot and the ball need to touch?
A fridge magnet pulls a metal door without touching it. What kind of force is this?
Which of these forces can act at a distance?

Which object can a magnet pull across a gap?
Which group does a cat belong to?
Living things can be grouped by what they look like and how they do what?
cards.reason: The question is garbled and cannot be answered as written; "how they live" is only one reading, and a pupil could defend "Sleep" (grouping by behaviour).

cards.question: Which feature would you use to group birds together?

cards.question: Where do vibrations from sound go first in the ear?

cards.key: No, the loop is no longer complete

cards.question: Which of these is a complete loop with a battery?
cards.key: A battery, a lamp and wires joined end to end

cards.question: Which word describes a circuit with a gap in it?
Which part of a plant makes the seeds?
What does a bee help move from flower to flower?
Frogs lay eggs in water. What is this called?
How do many plants spread their seeds to new places?
Which animal grows from a tiny egg into an adult in a process called metamorphosis?
Which material would be best for a bucket that holds water?
Why are metal saucepans used for cooking?
cards.key: They let heat pass through quickly

cards.question: Which material is best for a window in a house?
Why is wood used to make a table?
cards.key: It is strong and does not break easily

cards.question: Which material would be best for a spoon for hot soup?
What shape is the sun?
What shape is the Earth?
Which word best describes the shape of the moon?
Why are the sun, Earth and moon round?
cards.key: Gravity pulls them evenly from all sides

cards.question: Which one is the best example of a sphere?
What is a fossil?
cards.key: The remains or traces of something that once lived

cards.question: What usually has to happen to a plant or animal before a fossil can form?
cards.key: It is buried quickly in mud or sand

cards.question: Where do most fossils form?
cards.key: In layers of sediment at the bottom of water

cards.question: Over millions of years, what happens to the buried sediment?
cards.key: It is pressed and hardens into rock

cards.question: Which part of a fossil story helps scientists know how old it is?
cards.key: The layers of rock it was found in
